text.arabic_uthmani: ثُمَّ لَنَنزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عِتِيًّۭا

words.gloss_range: sequential and escalatory connector marking a distinct later stage
words.prose: {{ar:ثُمَّ}} ({{tr:thumma}}) does not merely add another statement. It opens 19:69 as a later and escalated stage after the gathering and presentation of 19:68, so extraction is heard as the next procedural act rather than a restatement of the prior scene. Its compact doubled sound also makes the hinge self-contained before the emphatic extraction verb enters, and the ayah then moves from the extraction act to the source phrase and finally to the identifying criterion.

topics.headline: escalated sequence stage
topics.summary: The opening particle marks extraction as a distinct later stage after the prior mass scene.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 19:69 advances the sworn procedure from gathered presentation into a new act of sorting.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as sequential and escalatory, and the boundary rows coherently read the ayah as continuing the oath-chain from 19:68.

topics.headline: audible hinge before extraction
topics.summary: The closed particle sound gives the transition an audible pause before the heavier verb.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first word as a compact hinge, not a loose glide into the extraction clause.
topics.reason: The shaddah and nasal closure are local surface facts; the claim is kept as sound-texture support rather than made the main parse.

topics.headline: act to source to criterion
topics.summary: The opening particle leads into a two-beat clause: extraction from each faction, then identification by severity.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the ayah is built as staged movement: act first, group-source next, criterion last.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence separates the extraction clause and the embedded identifying clause, matching the CRITICAL architecture claim.

words.gloss_range: oath-emphatic proclitic bound to the extraction verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the emphatic extraction verb to which the lām is bound

words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la-}}) carries the prior oath frame into the new verb without restating the oath object. Joined to {{ar:نَنزِعَنَّ}} ({{tr:nanzaʿanna}}), it works with the heavy final nūn so certainty is built into the word-shape itself, starting at the verb's first audible edge before the root consonants arrive. The extraction is therefore not a plain future report but the third sworn predicate in the chain that began in 19:68.

topics.headline: inherited oath chain
topics.summary: The lām continues the prior oath answer rather than beginning an independent announcement.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the certainty of 19:69 is inherited across the ayah boundary from the oath sequence in 19:68.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as emphatic or oath lām and as part of the triple oath sequence, so the CRITICAL cross-boundary reading is locally supported.

topics.headline: stacked verb emphasis
topics.summary: The lām and heavy nūn make certainty part of the extraction verb's form.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears inescapability as morphology, not as an added explanatory adverb.
topics.reason: The input explicitly marks lām and heavy energetic nūn as surface force that translation should preserve.

topics.headline: compressed onset of certainty
topics.summary: The one-letter proclitic places oath force at the first edge of the verb.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees how a single attached letter makes the verb begin under oath pressure.
topics.reason: The particle is a visible proclitic, and the rows' form claim is limited to its local attachment to the verb.

words.gloss_range: sworn first-person plural imperfect of forcible extraction, governing a source phrase and identifying clause
words.root_gloss_range: pulling out, wrenching, stripping, and removing by force are locally relevant; unrelated broader removal uses are only background

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: embedded selector clause governed by the extraction verb

words.prose: {{ar:نَنزِعَنَّ}} ({{tr:nanzaʿanna}}) is the engine of the ayah: a divine first-person imperfect enclosed by oath force and the heavy energetic ending. Its root gives the sorting a tactile pull or wrench, so the worst are not merely named but drawn out from within their factional setting. The repeated nasals, final ʿayn constriction, and doubled nūn let the word sound pressed at the same moment it names wrenching. The verb governs both the partitive source phrase and the embedded {{ar:أَيُّهُمْ}} ({{tr:ayyuhum}}) clause, making grammar enact extraction through layered reach. The same root can recall stripping sovereignty in 3:26 and extracting a witness from every nation in 28:75, but here those echoes are narrowed to punitive faction-by-faction selection against the mercy-name.

topics.headline: emphatic divine verb
topics.summary: The verb carries divine agency and sworn future certainty in one compact form.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the extraction's certainty is grammatically built into the verb, not supplied only by context.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the local form as an imperfect divine verb with lām and heavy energetic nūn, preserving the CRITICAL force claim.

topics.headline: forcible extraction image
topics.summary: The root presents sorting as wrenching embedded persons out of their groups.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels divine sorting as forceful removal from a factional body rather than as neutral classification.
topics.reason: The local verb is transitive with a source phrase, and the root evidence supports forcible pulling or stripping as the active branch.

topics.headline: layered argument reach
topics.summary: The verb reaches through the source phrase to an embedded identifying clause.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the syntax perform the extraction: source first, then the clause that identifies who is taken.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces both the source complement and the governed embedded clause under the extraction verb.

topics.headline: extraction echoes narrowed
topics.summary: Other extraction scenes clarify sovereign removal and witness-selection patterns without replacing the local punitive sorting.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this extraction belongs to a wider Quranic pattern of God drawing someone out, while 19:69 turns the pattern toward the worst rebels in each faction.
topics.reason: The intertextual rows give concrete parallels in 3:26 and 28:75; local syntax narrows them to an analogy of extraction, not a transfer of kingship or testimony into 19:69.

topics.headline: sound pressure of wrenching
topics.summary: The consonant cluster, throat consonant, and doubled nūn reinforce the forceful verb.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears pressure in the verb at the same point the word names wrenching extraction.
topics.reason: The sound claim is anchored in the local letters and gemination and is kept subordinate to the grammatical and lexical reading.

words.gloss_range: source and partitive preposition governing the every-faction phrase

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: selector reached after the source phrase

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the extraction come from within each faction, not toward a destination and not out of the groups wholesale. Its partitive source force lets the ayah say that every faction yields selected persons while still distinguishing those persons from the whole group. Because the phrase stands between the verb and {{ar:أَيُّهُمْ}} ({{tr:ayyuhum}}), the reader must pass through the group-source frame before the selected subset is identified.

topics.headline: partitive source
topics.summary: The preposition marks extraction from within every faction rather than total removal of factions.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that judgment penetrates each faction while selecting a subset from it.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following phrase the source complement of the extraction verb, and QAC explicitly marks partitive force.

topics.headline: visible source boundary
topics.summary: The separate preposition gives the source phrase a visible boundary between verb and selector.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the source phrase as its own syntactic checkpoint before the identifying clause arrives.
topics.reason: The preposition is a separate word and the phrase is positioned between the extraction verb and its embedded object clause.

words.gloss_range: singular construct quantifier meaning every or each in a distributive source phrase
words.root_gloss_range: totality and exhaustiveness are local; unrelated senses of fatigue or encircling are not activated here

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: faction noun governed by the construct quantifier

words.prose: {{ar:كُلِّ}} ({{tr:kulli}}) makes the source phrase exhaustive and distributive: each faction, one by one, comes under the same sorting procedure. Its construct binding to {{ar:شِيعَةٍ}} ({{tr:shīʿatin}}) keeps totality tied to the category of faction rather than to an unnamed mass. Against 30:32, where each faction is pleased with what it has, the same every-faction field becomes exposure rather than self-satisfaction. This same-surah field can also be heard against 19:93, where all come to the mercy-name as servants, and against 19:26, where a single vow is directed to the same name; here totality becomes collective exposure before that universal movement.

topics.headline: distributive every faction
topics.summary: The singular construct quantifier makes every faction yield its own selected extreme.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no factional category sits outside the sorting, yet the procedure works one faction at a time.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support genitive construct totality governed by the partitive source phrase.

topics.headline: construct-bound totality
topics.summary: The bound form makes totality depend directly on the following faction noun.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the word's exhaustiveness is not abstract; it is grammatically fastened to factional grouping.
topics.reason: The phrase is a forced construct relation, so the CRITICAL claim about bound totality survives locally.

topics.headline: totality echoes in the surah
topics.summary: The totalizing word links factional exposure to wider same-surah movement toward the mercy-name.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the every-faction sorting in 19:69 sits inside a surah arc that moves from individual devotion to universal servitude before the mercy-name.
topics.reason: The echoes to 19:26 and 19:93 are concrete and meaningful, but they are kept as same-surah resonance rather than as the local grammar of the quantifier.

topics.headline: factional complacency reversed
topics.summary: The every-faction phrase reverses the self-satisfied factional scene of 30:32.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees factional confidence turned into exposure: each party's self-satisfaction in 30:32 becomes each faction's vulnerability in 19:69.
topics.reason: The row gives a concrete lexical parallel in 30:32; local syntax limits it to contrastive echo.

words.gloss_range: indefinite faction, party, or sect as the genitive complement of every
words.root_gloss_range: following, party-affiliation, factional grouping, and divisive fragmentation are locally relevant; neutral crowd language is too weak

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: construct quantifier governing the faction noun

words.prose: {{ar:شِيعَةٍ}} ({{tr:shīʿatin}}) completes the source phrase as an indefinite faction, not a neutral crowd. The word's following-and-party field makes the group a tangible social body from which persons can be pulled out, while Quranic usage such as 6:159 and 30:32 gives it fragmentation pressure and 28:15 shows the party-loyalty side of the same field. Its indefiniteness under {{ar:كُلِّ}} ({{tr:kulli}}) keeps the category open: not one named sect, but any factional identity that falls under the universal sorting. The indefinite ending also anticipates the final indefinite rebellion-quality, linking the group-source to the closing diagnosis by cadence.

topics.headline: open faction category
topics.summary: The indefinite singular noun lets every factional instance fall under the source phrase.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not target one named group but opens the class of factional grouping itself.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun indefinite and genitive after the construct quantifier; attachment evidence makes it complete the source phrase.

topics.headline: faction not neutral group
topics.summary: The noun selects party or sect identity with fragmentation pressure.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the source as factional identity, not simply human grouping.
topics.reason: QAC explicitly notes divisive religious fragmentation, and the CRITICAL rows' faction/sect semantics fit the local noun.

topics.headline: extractable social body
topics.summary: The concrete noun shape lets the faction function as a body from which persons are removed.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees factional affiliation as an embodied container, not an abstract label.
topics.reason: The noun is tagged concrete and stands inside the source phrase governed by the extraction verb.

topics.headline: faction echoes narrowed
topics.summary: Concrete echoes to factional complacency and party loyalty illuminate the noun without governing the local scene.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same faction word can mark religious fragmentation in 6:159, self-satisfied parties in 30:32, and social loyalty in 28:15, while 19:69 makes faction the source of judgment.
topics.reason: The references are concrete, but local grammar keeps the noun as the source complement, so the echoes are contrastive and not alternate local senses.

topics.headline: indefinite cadence
topics.summary: The indefinite ending anticipates the later indefinite rebellion-quality.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the group-source and final moral quality connected by a shared indefinite cadence.
topics.reason: The claim is limited to local sound patterning between the indefinite faction noun and the final accusative gerund.

words.gloss_range: which-of-them selector, with attached plural suffix, heading the embedded identifying clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: accepted accusative variant exposing direct government

words.prose: {{ar:أَيُّهُمْ}} ({{tr:ayyuhum}}) turns the extraction into identification: which of them, or the one of them who, is most severe. The attached suffix keeps the selected persons tied to the already gathered population and to the members of each faction. The standard surface permits a debated indirect-question reading, while the accepted accusative variant {{ar:أَيَّهُمْ}} ({{tr:ayyahum}}) makes direct government by the extraction verb more visible; either way, the verb reaches a whole embedded criterion clause rather than a simple noun.

topics.headline: suffix-bound selector
topics.summary: The attached plural suffix restricts the selector to the gathered and factional population already in scope.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the selection is from the known gathered them, not an open-ended whoever.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the suffix as the genitive domain of the selector, and boundary rows tie that suffix back to the prior gathered crowd.

topics.headline: embedded object clause
topics.summary: The selector heads the identifying clause governed by the extraction verb.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine extraction operating through a criterion clause, not a bare object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence syntactically forces the full selector-predicate sequence as the clausal complement selected by the verb.

topics.headline: qiraat parse contrast
topics.summary: The accepted case contrast clarifies indirect-question versus accusative relative pressure without displacing the aligned surface.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same selector can stage either question-resolving identification or direct targeting, while the local standard wording remains the aligned form.
topics.reason: The variant is valid contrastive evidence, but the output keeps the standard local surface and uses the variant only to expose syntactic pressure.

topics.headline: forensic register shift
topics.summary: The ayah moves from mass declaration into a judicial identifying criterion.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the discourse shift from proclaimed outcome into forensic selection.
topics.reason: The local clause structure supports a move from the main sworn clause into the embedded identifying clause.

words.gloss_range: elative predicate meaning most severe or most intense, completed by the rebellion tamyiz
words.root_gloss_range: hardness, intensity, severity, and tightening are relevant as degree pressure; physical strength branches remain contrastive unless specified by the local tamyiz

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: final accusative specification naming the domain of severity
adversative preposition directing severity toward its target

words.prose: {{ar:أَشَدُّ}} ({{tr:ashaddu}}) is the predicate that turns the selector into a ranked criterion. It is not absolute severity: {{ar:عِتِيًّا}} ({{tr:ʿitiyyā}}) later specifies the domain as rebellion, while {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) directs that severity against the mercy-name. The hardness field of the root and the doubled consonant make the ranking feel morally and acoustically heavy. Echoes such as 48:29, 41:15, and the punishment intensity of 20:127 sharpen the inversion: intensity that can be rightful against enemies, boasted as power, or named of punishment becomes, here, defiant severity against mercy.

topics.headline: elative ranked criterion
topics.summary: The elative predicate ranks the selected persons by degree.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah selects the extreme edge within each faction, not everyone who belongs to a faction.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as an elative predicate inside the embedded selector clause.

topics.headline: tamyiz fixes the domain
topics.summary: The final accusative gerund specifies the respect in which severity is measured.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader waits for the final word to learn that the ranking is severity in rebellion, not strength or punishment.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence strongly licenses the final gerund as accusative specification of the elative.

topics.headline: hardness and sound
topics.summary: The root and doubled consonant give the criterion a hardened feel.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears and feels severity as hardened intensity, not as a flat comparative label.
topics.reason: The local elative belongs to the severity root, and the doubled consonant is part of the surface form.

topics.headline: severity echoes narrowed
topics.summary: Parallels to rightful harshness, boasted strength, and punishment intensity sharpen the local moral inversion.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 19:69 redirects familiar severity language toward the specific moral problem of rebellion against mercy.
topics.reason: The concrete references to 48:29, 41:15, and 20:127 are useful contrasts, while local grammar keeps the active domain as rebellion specified by the final gerund.

words.gloss_range: adversative-directional preposition, against or over, governing the mercy-name

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: mercy-name governed as the adversative target
elative predicate modified by the adversative phrase
final rebellion noun after the adversative target

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) makes the severity directional and adversarial. It governs {{ar:ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-raḥmāni}}) and attaches that target to {{ar:أَشَدُّ}} ({{tr:ashaddu}}), so the measure is not free-floating intensity but hostility aimed at the mercy-name. Its upward or over-against force adds arrogance pressure, and its placement before {{ar:عِتِيًّا}} ({{tr:ʿitiyyā}}) makes the target of defiance arrive before the final diagnosis is named.

topics.headline: adversative targeting
topics.summary: The preposition directs severity against the mercy-name rather than marking neutral location.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the offense is measured by its target: hostility is aimed against the mercy-name.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the preposition to govern the divine name as complement of the elative, supporting an adversative target relation.

topics.headline: arrogance pressure
topics.summary: The upward/against force lets rebellion sound like hostile elevation over mercy.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the preposition itself add arrogance to the direction of rebellion.
topics.reason: QAC explicitly notes adversative-directional force and arrogance-connotation; the 48:29 contrast is kept as moral inversion, not local replacement.

topics.headline: target before diagnosis
topics.summary: The PP names the target before the final rebellion noun supplies the domain.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears who the severity is against before hearing the final word that names rebellion.
topics.reason: The local word order places the adversative PP between the elative and the final accusative specification.

topics.headline: misassigned extremity echo
topics.summary: The 19:8 extremity contrast belongs to the severity and rebellion words, not to this preposition.
topics.no_reader_payoff_reason: The row gives a useful 19:8 contrast, but it has no distinct payoff for the preposition after the final rebellion word accounts for that echo.
topics.reason: The row concerns the severity and rebellion lexemes rather than the local function of {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}), so it is preserved in coverage but not repeated in this word's prose.

words.gloss_range: definite divine mercy-name governed as the adversative target
words.root_gloss_range: mercy, compassion, protective kinship, and the intensive divine name are relevant; generic abstract mercy alone is too weak
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ}} ({{tr:al-raḥmāni}}) is not a generic divine mention here; it is the definite mercy-name governed by the adversative preposition. The faʿlān form and the broader mercy family, including protective kinship/body pressure, make the target overwhelmingly marked by mercy, so rebellion becomes rebellion against mercy specifically. Because this name is a dominant refrain in Surah 19, the word also pulls the local offense into the surah's arc: prostration before the mercy-name in 19:58, universal servitude to the mercy-name in 19:93, and the opening memory of mercy in 19:2 all sharpen the perversity of being most severe against it. Its smooth assimilated article and flowing sound sit immediately before the harder rebellion closure, so the recitation itself presses mercy into defiance.

topics.headline: definite mercy target
topics.summary: The definite divine name is the governed target of adversarial severity.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the rebellion is aimed at a named divine mercy-title, not at an abstract idea or unnamed deity.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a definite proper divine name in the genitive after the preposition, and attachment evidence makes it the target of the elative frame.

topics.headline: mercy-name selection

topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the moral irony: the worst severity is directed against the name most marked by mercy.
topics.reason: The local noun is the mercy-name rather than another divine title, and its position before the final rebellion word makes that selection decisive.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices fullness and protective mercy pressure in the name while still reading it as a proper divine title.
topics.reason: The broader root family informs the resonance, but QAC and V4 local form observations keep the local word as a proper noun.

topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete same-surah references in 19:58 and 19:93, and QAC notes the name's dominance in Surah 19.

topics.headline: mercy-rebellion sound closure

topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the mercy-name immediately press into the hard final diagnosis of rebellion.
topics.reason: The local word order places the divine name directly before the final gerund, while the sound claims are anchored to the local surface.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative gerund specifying extreme defiant rebellion
words.root_gloss_range: exceeding bounds, insolence, hardening, and violent excess are locally relevant; ordinary sin or disagreement is too weak

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: elative predicate specified by the final gerund
accepted vowel variant preserving the gerund role

words.prose: {{ar:عِتِيًّۭا}} ({{tr:ʿitiyyā}}) closes the ayah by naming the domain in which the selected persons are worst. As an accusative tamyīz, it specifies {{ar:أَشَدُّ}} ({{tr:ashaddu}}): the ranking is not power, number, or punishment, but extreme defiant rebellion. The root carries excess and hardening, so the final word feels like a moral rigidity; the identical form in 19:8 lets bodily extremity and moral extremity speak to each other, while the raging-wind use in 69:6 keeps uncontrolled-force pressure in the root field without replacing the local moral sense. Its rare gerund shape, accepted vowel variant {{ar:عُتِيًّا}} ({{tr:ʿutiyyan}}), and echo with the prior -iyyā ending in 19:68 make the closure both diagnostic and rhythmic. The punishment logic of 65:8 and the mercy-name's extension in 19:75 remain echoes around the word, while the local function stays the diagnostic criterion of 19:69.

topics.headline: tamyiz diagnostic domain
topics.summary: The final accusative gerund specifies the respect in which the selected persons are most severe.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader waits until the last word to learn that the sorting criterion is rebellion itself.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence strongly licenses the word as the accusative specification of the elative, including across the intervening prepositional phrase.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final diagnosis as excessive defiant rebellion against mercy, not generic sin.
topics.reason: The lexical evidence supports exceeding bounds and insolent rebellion, and the local construction makes that quality the measure of severity.

topics.headline: bodily and moral hardening

topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give an exact same-form same-surah echo in 19:8; local grammar keeps the active sense in 19:69 moral rather than bodily.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees how the word's rare form and vowel variation intensify the closure while preserving the same gerund function.
topics.reason: The variant changes the initial vowel but not the local gerundial tamyīz role, so the topic is preserved as narrowed form evidence.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that rebellion is framed as a quality-scale for classification, not as a narrated act.
topics.reason: The form is an indefinite accusative gerund and locally functions as the specification of the elative.

topics.headline: punishment and mercy echoes

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the quality named here anticipates judgment logic like 65:8 and sits beside the mercy-name's extension in 19:75.
topics.reason: The concrete references to 65:8 and 19:75 are meaningful echoes, but local grammar keeps the word as the present ayah's diagnostic tamyīz.

topics.headline: boundary rhyme closure
topics.summary: The final cadence links prior kneeling posture to inner rebellion.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the move from bodies brought kneeling in 19:68 to inner rebellion diagnosed at the end of 19:69.
topics.reason: The boundary rows give the concrete 19:68 cadence link, and the local word is the ayah-final closure.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses that the rebellion word belongs to a wider root field of excess and uncontrolled force.
topics.reason: The 69:6 wind reference shows root-field force, but local syntax selects moral rebellion as the final criterion.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction at words 2-10 extracts from every shiyah whichever member is most intense in itiyy.
baseline_models.mechanism: Each shiyah is a support-bound following. N-z-a forcefully separates an embedded member, while the comparative ranks the faction internally by hardened departure from obedience. The act exposes an extreme node rather than treating the faction as an undifferentiated mass.

activation_trace.role: Uprooting a thing from its settled place supplies forceful separation of an embedded faction member.
Encompassing all parts makes the operation recur across every faction without remainder.
A supporting follower-group supplies the social unit whose internal maximum is selected.
Strength, hardness, and severity supply the comparative scale.
Haughty departure from obedience specifies what the comparison maximizes.

changed_reading.before: The worst people are selected from sects.
changed_reading.after: From every support-bound faction, its most hardened rebel is forcibly singled out, exposing an internal maximum rather than condemning a flat collective.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The predicate at words 7-10 places intensified itiyy specifically against al-Rahman.
baseline_models.mechanism: The predicate overlays a tightened hardness onto active departure from obedience, with mercy and tenderness as its explicit counter-pole. The offense is relational: resistance hardens against mercy's claim rather than floating as generic misconduct.

activation_trace.role: Tightening a bond supplies the image of resistance made fast and difficult to loosen.
Tenderness, mercy, and beneficence specify the relation against which the resistance is directed.
Haughty departure from obedience keeps the hardening anchored in active refusal.

changed_reading.before: They are extremely disobedient toward God.
changed_reading.after: Their extremity is a self-fastened refusal directed specifically against mercy and beneficence.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The superlative force of word 7 modifies the terminal-state potential of itiyy at word 10.
baseline_models.mechanism: The terminal-state branch of itiyy, intensified by the hardness comparative, permits a temporal model: selection falls on the most calcified endpoint of rebellion, not merely the loudest current offender.

activation_trace.role: Hardness and severity supply degree to the terminal condition.
Old age and a terminal condition beyond repair supply calcification as an endpoint image, not a literal age claim.

changed_reading.before: The selection measures present intensity of rebellion.
changed_reading.after: The selection may measure rebellion that has matured into its most terminal and resistant state.

context_deltas.mechanism: The preceding replacement generation follows desires repeatedly. This revises shiyah from a merely static party into a reproduced following-chain whose extreme member crystallizes and can transmit accumulated drift.

activation_trace.role: Following and accompanying supply the focus faction's chain of imitation.
Uprooting from a settled place breaks one member out of that transmitted formation.
One thing replacing another supplies the generational succession in which the formation is reproduced.
Following in another's track supplies the behavioral link that forms the chain.
Desire renewed after desire supplies the repeated motive that deepens the drift.

structural_cues: 19:59 places replacement, neglect, and following before 19:69's extraction from every faction; 19:60's exception prevents a deterministic ancestry reading.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies succession, following, and repeated desire; I infer that affiliation can be reproduced by imitation. A live alternative is that shiyah denotes only synchronic parties.

changed_reading.before: A faction is a static membership container.
changed_reading.after: A faction can be a generational chain of imitation, and extraction exposes the member in whom its inherited drift has hardened most.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context names al-Rahman as promise-giver to servants and then commands worship. The focus opposition is therefore a refusal of a mercy-servanthood relation whose offered side has already been displayed.

activation_trace.role: A tightened bond supplies resistance made fast against the contextual relation.
Departure from obedience supplies the refusal side of that relation.
Mercy and beneficence identify the promise-giver before the same title becomes the focus counter-pole.
A promise that opens hope supplies the offered good against which refusal hardens.
Humble worship supplies the relational posture that focus itiyy rejects.

structural_cues: Al-Rahman recurs at 19:61 and 19:69, while servant language at 19:61 becomes an imperative to worship at 19:65.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mercy, promise, servanthood, and worship; I read the focus preposition as relational resistance to that offer. Alternatively, the divine title may identify its referent without carrying the full contrast.

changed_reading.before: The verse ranks generic defiance toward the deity.
changed_reading.after: It ranks a hardened repudiation of the merciful lord-servant relation already framed by promise and worship.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence first drives the whole company to a destination and forces it present, then extracts each faction's maximum, then assigns priority for contact with fire. Extraction functions as staged exposure and ordering rather than random seizure.

activation_trace.role: Uprooting from place supplies the central selective movement after assembly.
The supporting group supplies the repeated compartments within the assembled whole.
Driving and gathering a group toward a destination supplies the mass assembly before extraction.
Presence, witnessing, and proximity place the gathered company at the selection site.
Priority and entitlement turn the extracted maximum into an ordered first claim.
Meeting fire and its heat supplies the destination of that priority.

structural_cues: The repeated thumma sequence across 19:68, 19:69, and 19:70 orders gathering, extraction, and knowledgeable prioritization.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies ordered gathering, forced presence, extraction, and priority for fire; I infer a triage-like staging. Alternatively, extraction may only isolate cases for separate judgment without implying a queue.

changed_reading.before: The most rebellious are simply identified.
changed_reading.after: After total assembly, every faction yields its maximum into a visible priority order for exposure to fire.

context_deltas.mechanism: All successively arrive; then the protected are saved by separation while wrongdoers are left kneeling. This polarity makes the earlier extraction of the worst an exposure move distinct from the later rescue-extraction.

activation_trace.role: Uprooting supplies an ambiguous separation whose direction is clarified by the later polarity.
Advancing and entering in succession supplies the common arrival from which opposed separations operate.
Deliverance by separation reserves the rescue direction for the protected.
Placing oneself within protection identifies the class moved by rescue.
Leaving a thing in place supplies the opposite fate of the wrongdoers.
Kneeling fixes the left-behind class in the posture introduced before focus.

structural_cues: 19:71 universalizes arrival; 19:72's balanced verbs save one class and leave the other, with kneeling repeated from 19:68.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies common arrival and an explicit rescue-versus-leave contrast; I infer that 19:69 foregrounds the worst rather than releasing them. A live alternative is that the two separations are independent acts with no paired choreography.

changed_reading.before: Being pulled out could sound like release from the gathered mass.
changed_reading.after: The worst are pulled forward for exposure; rescue is a later, oppositely directed separation reserved for the protected.

context_deltas.mechanism: A human boast ranks two parties by better station and assembly; the focus substitutes maximal rebellion as the diagnostic; the sequence then returns worse station and weaker host. The same comparative social field is reversed from public prestige to exposed resistance.

activation_trace.role: A mutually strengthening follower-group supplies the social formation whose prestige is remeasured.
Strength and hardness replace visible prestige as the comparison's hidden moral axis.
A separated faction or flock supplies the two-party unit in the challengers' boast.
Station and residence supply the first visible prestige metric.
The council where a group assembles supplies the second visible prestige metric.
Badness and harm reverse the earlier claim of being better.
The opposite of strength reverses the factions' implied social power.
A mutually supporting host returns factional solidarity as an exposed weakness.

structural_cues: The comparative arc runs from better station and better assembly in 19:73, through most intense rebellion in 19:69's governing scene, to worse station and weaker host in 19:75.
19:74 inserts past generations with superior goods and appearance, undercutting visible success as a stable measure.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies mirrored faction nouns, comparatives, station, assembly, and host; I infer that the focus comparison answers and reverses the boast. Alternatively, these may be adjacent but independent comparisons.

changed_reading.before: The divine selection uses an independent moral scale unrelated to factional self-presentation.
changed_reading.after: The selection exposes what factional prestige was measuring badly: the apparently better assembly can be the formation most hardened against mercy and headed toward worse standing.

context_deltas.mechanism: Al-Rahman extends time for one in straying, while guidance is increased for the guided. These opposed trajectories strengthen a temporal reading of the focus maximum: itiyy can be an accrued, prolonged calcification rather than an innate fixed type.

activation_trace.role: A terminal condition beyond repair supplies the endpoint whose history context can now expose.
Hardness and severity supply the degree accumulated at that endpoint.
Deviation from guidance supplies the trajectory along which extension occurs.
A term or span made long supplies time in which the deviating state can persist.
Mercy is the named extender here and the explicit counter-pole of focus resistance.
Increase and growth supply the contrasting positive trajectory.
Gentle direction toward the right path specifies what grows on the opposite trajectory.

structural_cues: 19:75 repeats extension around the one in straying; 19:76 immediately answers with increase in guidance.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies prolonged straying and increased guidance; I infer that focus intensity can register an accrued endpoint. The text does not state that extension causes rebellion, and the comparative may rank only present conduct.

changed_reading.before: The terminal hardening model describes a fixed offender type.
changed_reading.after: The hardest offender may be the endpoint of a prolonged trajectory, contrasted with an equally dynamic growth in guidance.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the undivided-property branch is remote from the ordinary group noun. It remains anchored in the focus shiyah and n-z-a branches and is activated by inheritance at 19:63; downstream prose should present it only as a legal-material analogy, never as a replacement translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The combination of extraction at word 2, every at word 4, and shiyah at word 5 permits a partition image.

activation_trace.role: An undivided share in common property supplies the faction as a collectively held block.
Uprooting and removal supply the act that partitions one exposed share from the block.
Comprehensive totality makes the partitioning operation apply to each collective holding.
Property passing from predecessor to heir activates the nearby legal field of shares and partition.

changed_reading.before: Each faction simply yields one member.
changed_reading.after: As a contained legal analogy, each faction resembles an undivided holding whose most resistant share is partitioned out, dissolving collective cover.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because shiyah ordinarily names a social faction, and the spark branch at 19:75 is especially form-remote. It remains valid as a material analogy through the focus fire-stoking branch and 19:70's explicit fire contact; prose should say the faction behaves like a stoking coalition, not translate it as fuel or assert literal causation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Shiyah at word 5 has a fire-stoking branch, while extraction and maximal intensity remain explicit at words 2 and 7.

activation_trace.role: Feeding wood to strengthen a fire supplies the faction as a coalition that intensifies a shared blaze.
Strength and severity supply the degree to which the collective blaze is intensified.
Uprooting supplies removal of the principal stoker from the coalition.
Meeting fire and its heat gives the material analogy a visible contextual destination.
Flying sparks provide a deliberately distant reinforcing echo for the stoked-fire image.

changed_reading.before: Factions are only containers from which severe members are selected.
changed_reading.after: As a contained material analogy, each faction is a stoking coalition whose fiercest intensifier is pulled forward to meet the fire.

strongest_changes: The verse became a staged intra-faction extraction inside a gather-present-prioritize sequence, not a free-standing statement about generic worst people.
The comparative reverses the factions' own better-station and better-assembly boast into a measure of rebellion followed by worse station and weaker host.
The later rescue-versus-leave polarity makes extraction of the worst an exposure move, while extended straying makes their hardness potentially accrued rather than fixed.
summary.what_was_special: The packet activated a social topology: factions are support structures, imitation chains, and prestige assemblies whose collective cover is broken by individual extraction. The title al-Rahman made the ranked offense specifically anti-mercy.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus does not establish that the extracted maximum is a leader or causal representative rather than simply the most extreme member.
The extension in 19:75 may permit hardening without causing it; the temporal arrow remains reader-supplied.
The partition and fire-stoking models are analogies and must not displace the ordinary social sense of shiyah.

baseline.text: Sonra her gruptan Rahman'a karşı en çok başkaldıranı mutlaka çekip çıkaracağız.

findings.text: Her destek grubundan en katı başkaldıranın çekilmesi, topluluğun sorumluluğu dağıtmak yerine bireysel direnci görünür kılan bir ayıklama alanı olduğunu gösterir.
